terms.gloss: egg foam: whites beaten stiff with sugar and baked
terms.comment: A description of ours. We have found no word for meringue in Lewis & Short, Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Spūma is the classical word for foam and froth (see “foam”); the whites are albūmina (see “egg white”).

phrases.latin: Albūmina cum saccharō peragitā, dōnec spūma dēnsa fīat.
phrases.english: Whisk the whites with the sugar until the meringue is thick.

phrases.latin: Spūmam ōvōrum in crustum impōne et in furnum conde, dōnec flāvēscat.
phrases.english: Spread the meringue on the pie and put it in the oven until it turns golden.

sources: Lewis & Short: spuma · Lewis & Short: ovum
